title: Frequency Response of Amplifiers
intro: Gain at DC is only half the story. Device and load capacitances create poles and zeros that set how fast each amplifier can run, and speed trades with gain, power and noise. This chapter follows Razavi, Chapter 6.

items: Miller effect and poles: Miller's theorem and its limits, one pole per node, $f_T \approx g_m/(2\pi C_{GS})$.
CS stage: Miller estimate, the exact second-order response, the dominant-pole approximation, the RHP zero at $g_m/C_{GD}$, input impedance.
Source follower: LHP zero, bootstrapped input capacitance, negative input resistance, inductive output impedance.
Common-gate stage: no Miller effect, effect of $r_o$ and of gate resistance.
Cascode: three poles, why $C_{GD1}$ is multiplied by only about 2.
Differential pairs: CMRR against frequency, the mirror pole and its LHP zero.
Gain-bandwidth trade-offs: $\mathrm{GBW} = g_m/(2\pi C_L)$, bandwidth shrinkage of cascaded stages.
Time-constant methods: zero-value time constants and the extra element theorem.

blocks.text: Rule of thumb for any stage: find each node's resistance and capacitance to ground, split bridging capacitors with Miller's approximation (checking the gain they really see), and the lowest $1/(RC)$ is your bandwidth estimate.
